messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#780] GLM and GLMER using RMR
parts:
On Jun 5, 2013 8:26 AM, "Sanjeev Taran" <sanjee...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Is GLM and GLMER a good fit for rmr?

Could you elaborate on what you mean by "fit"?
>
> I want to do a logit regression of longitudinal data and my formula is like  y ~ x1 + x2 + x1:x2 + (x1 | x3). The variables in the bracket are for mixed effects. I don't know how to implement this is map reduce. The example, I see with RMR does not allow one to put in a formula like the one I have. Please advise!
>

It is just an example so it doesn't aim for the quality standards of a library function. In particular it doesn't offer a formula interface. As a general guide, the supported functionality is covered in the help documentation. Everything else is learning materials, benchmarks, tests or internal functions.

Antonio

> Thanks.
> -Sanjeev

messages.subject: Re: GLM and GLMER using RMR
parts:
Thank you for your reply. What i mean by "fit" is whether MR is the correct programming paradigm to solve the regression problem. 
If the answer is yes, I would like to know whether I can use the standard stat package from R for the stat functions using MR.  I wanted to use the formula interface. In other words, since I do not know the inner workings of GLMER, do I have to recode the inner algorithm for glmer to use it alongwith RMR.
Please advise.
Thanks.
On Tuesday, June 4, 2013 5:19:01 PM UTC-7, Sanjeev Taran wrote:
Is GLM and GLMER a good fit for rmr?

I want to do a logit regression of longitudinal data and my formula is like  y ~ x1 + x2 + x1:x2 + (x1 | x3). The variables in the bracket are for mixed effects. I don't know how to implement this is map reduce. The example, I see with RMR does not allow one to put in a formula like the one I have. Please advise!

On Jun 5, 2013 6:06 PM, "Sanjeev Taran" <sanjee...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thank you for your reply. What i mean by "fit" is whether MR is the correct programming paradigm to solve the regression problem.
I know it can be done. Other than that I don't think I can say much.
> If the answer is yes, I would like to know whether I can use the standard stat package from R for the stat functions using MR.
I wanted to use the formula interface. In other words, since I do not know the inner workings of GLMER, do I have to recode the inner algorithm for glmer to use it alongwith RMR.

Worse than that. If you recode the same algorithm, you'll miss the benefits of Mr.
You need to write an algorithm for the Mr model.
